race_name: We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo

top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo. Practice on belgian cobblestones and short steep bergs: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 153 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
153 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
6,890ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on belgian cobblestones and short steep bergs can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo's belgian cobblestones and short steep bergs rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
At We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 6,890ft of climbing on belgian cobblestones and short steep bergs does to your power file on race day.
153 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 153 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo. Train it until it feels boring.

race_overlay.weather: April in Antwerp to Oudenaarde, Belgium — Early April in Flanders is the definition of hard-weather cycling. Temperatures range from 5-15C (41-59F), with rain a strong probability and wind a certainty across the flat Flemish plains. The cobblestones become treacherous when wet. This is Classics weather — you dress for the worst and hope for less. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 153 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 153 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at We Ride Flanders / Ronde van Vlaanderen Cyclo demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride belgian cobblestones and short steep bergs at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 153 miles of belgian cobblestones and short steep bergs in Antwerp to Oudenaarde, Belgium.
